# MKRECIPEDIR chooses where F recipes are written. Keywords pick a private
# directory (removed afterwards); a path puts the file directly there.
mkdir tmp xdg build
env TMPDIR=$WORK/tmp

# auto (the default) uses a private directory in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR if set...
env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$WORK/xdg
mk -p 1 where
stdout '^script=.*/xdg/mk-where-[^/]*/'
stdout '^dir=drwx------'
exec ls xdg
! stdout .

# ...and otherwise one in $TMPDIR
env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=
mk -p 1 where
stdout '^script=.*/tmp/mk-where-[^/]*/'
exec ls tmp
! stdout .

# tmp and xdg choose explicitly; xdg needs $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR
env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$WORK/xdg
mk -p 1 where MKRECIPEDIR=tmp
stdout '^script=.*/tmp/mk-where-'
env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=
! mk -p 1 where MKRECIPEDIR=xdg
stderr 'MKRECIPEDIR is xdg, but \$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is not set'

# a path puts a hidden file directly in that directory, so the script's
# directory is that directory
mk -p 1 where MKRECIPEDIR=./build
stdout '^script=\./build/\.mk-recipe-where-'
exec ls -a build
! stdout '\.mk-recipe'

# the setting can come from the mkfile, too
mk -p 1 -f local.mk where
stdout '^script=\./\.mk-recipe-where-'

# anything else is an error, so a typo does not silently pick a location
! mk -p 1 where MKRECIPEDIR=temp
stderr 'MKRECIPEDIR: unknown value "temp"'

-- mkfile --
where:VF:
	echo script=$$0
	echo dir=$$(ls -ld "$$(dirname "$$0")")
-- local.mk --
MKRECIPEDIR = .
where:VF:
	echo script=$$0
